items.title: 69537_Jimmy Jones oral history interview
items.q: I asked the late Arthur Logan, Ellington's doctor... And he gave me I guess possibly the most logical answer.

ctx.x: Well, there's a doctors' symphony here in Los Angeles, isn't there?

Yeah. It's quite an association, and I asked the late Arthur Logan, Ellington's doctor, you know, I said, 'Why?' And he gave me I guess possibly the most logical answer. He says, 'When you've got --,' especially jazz. He says, 'All of you guys can play the blues, but it's the matter of the man that takes the best solo.' And he says, 'Well, okay. We all read X-rays, and if a person needs surgery it's the man
that takes the best solo on surgery." And I said, "Well, gee, that's a great parallel."
